messages:
maria.engineering: hit a customer report — go get fails for our go-sdk after they upgraded to our tagged v3.0.0 release
alex.support: can you paste the exact error they see?
maria.engineering: sure, here's the go get output they sent: 
```
go: github.com/redwood/inference-go@v3.0.0: reading https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/redwood/inference-go/@v/v3.0.0.info: 404 Not Found
go: error loading module requirements
```
alex.support: 404 from GOPROXY usually means the tag doesn't match module path or the tag wasn't pushed to origin. did they use a replace in their module?
maria.engineering: customer says they didn't add any replace. their go.mod points to `github.com/redwood/inference-go v3.0.0`
tim.devops: quick checks: `git ls-remote --tags origin` on the sdk repo and `git show-ref --tags` locally. also `go mod download -json github.com/redwood/inference-go@v3.0.0` for more metadata
sam.eng: possible common cause: module path in go.mod inside repo still declares `module github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2` or missing /v3 suffix while tag is v3.0.0. Go requires module path to have major version suffix for v2+ when using semantic import versioning.
maria.engineering: oh nice call. customer ran `go env GOPROXY` and it's `https://proxy.golang.org,direct`
ci-bot: build-check: a previous publishing step failed to annotate the v3 tag with the correct module path (CI step `bump-version` aborted) :warning:
alex.support: can you reproduce quickly in a clean env and post commands?
maria.engineering: steps I ran locally: 
```
# clone the sdk tag
git clone https://github.com/redwood/inference-go.git && cd inference-go
git checkout v3.0.0
# inspect module line
sed -n '1,4p' go.mod
# try to fetch from proxy
go mod download -json github.com/redwood/inference-go@v3.0.0
```
sam.eng: what's the module line output?
maria.engineering: it's `module github.com/redwood/inference-go` (no /v3) which explains the 404 if clients try `github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3` vs tag mismatch. That repo was tagged v3.0.0 but the module path didn't follow semver import paths.
alex.support: consequence: when consumers do `require github.com/redwood/inference-go v3.0.0` the go tool expects module path `.../v3` inside the repo OR the tag to be a pseudo-version matching the root path. mismatch => proxy can't map.
tim.devops: fixes: (1) create a v3 module root by changing module line to `module github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3` and cut a patch tag v3.0.1 with updated go.mod; OR (2) maintain old module path and release v3 as a pseudo-style v0.x or keep the major at v1 semantics (not recommended).
sam.eng: alternative immediate workaround for customers: add a replace directive in their go.mod to point at the exact commit or private fork: `replace github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3 => github.com/redwood/inference-go v3.0.0` but that's messy. Better we republish.
maria.engineering: customer asked for a quick workaround while we fix tags. we suggested `GOPRIVATE=github.com/redwood` and `GONOSUMDB` but that's only if they have private access; not ideal for public releases.
alex.support: can we roll an emergency patch? who's owner of release pipeline? @sam.eng
sam.eng: I can cut a v3.0.1 tomorrow with corrected module line. in the meantime we should confirm whether any other tagged release suffered the same release-tool bug. I'll run a batch check across tags for module path vs tag suffix.
ci-bot: action created: GH issue #1245 release tool: missing module major-suffix on tagged releases (assigned to sam.eng)
maria.engineering: customer is on a tight deadline — asked if we can backport a v2 compatibility tag so their code can `require github.com/redwood/inference-go v2.3.0` and not change imports.
sam.eng: backporting isn't safe without compatibility guarantees. better route: we publish corrected v3 and offer temporary `replace` snippet and add a note in release notes. also offer them a small billing credit for time wasted.
alex.support: I've offered the customer the replace snippet plus a short walkthrough and escalated to sales for credits. they accepted the snippet and will try.
maria.engineering: adding repro log they can run so others can validate: 
```bash
export GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct
go clean -modcache
go get github.com/redwood/inference-go@v3.0.0  # expected 404 for bad tag
# after fix: go get github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3@v3.0.1
```
sam.eng: follow-ups: (1) run a script to check all repo tags vs go.mod module lines, (2) add a CI check on tag publish that validates module path major suffix for v2+, (3) prepare a changelog entry and customer email.
tim.devops: I'll put the CI hook in the release workflow and add a gating job that fails the tag release if mismatch detected.
alex.support: thanks all. customer will confirm if replace workaround works. will update thread when they respond. :thumbsup:
